title: Thorn and Spire
premise: Orsen Delacroix poisons herself nightly for the crown while secretly keeping the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, a smugglers' guild that trades in relics, memories, and last dragon-eggs. When a dying courier presses a map into her hands — a map to the Emberhold, where the final dragon-fire still burns — she becomes hunted by both the Crown and the Ashen Order, who want the fire extinguished forever. Guided by the map's ghostly cartographer, a memory bound into the parchment, Orsen discovers the fire is her own inheritance: her taster's immunity was bred from dragonblood generations ago. In the end, she must choose between giving the fire to the law that poisoned her or setting it free, reigniting the old war on new terms — one where dragons choose their allies.
about_author: August Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated heirlooms in a coastal customs house. They write fantasy about people who inherit burdens they never asked to carry.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen survives another poisoned banquet, then slips away to double-entry the Guild of Impossible Things' ledgers — including an entry for 'one ember, unspent.' Establishes her double life, her meticulous mind, and her quiet resentment of a crown that uses her body as a shield. Emotional beat: controlled dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Docks
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. A burned, dying courier finds her at the guild's dockside counting-house and presses a rolled map into her hands with the words 'it knows its own blood.' He dies as the Ashen Order's white-cloaks close in; Orsen escapes through the salt-cellars. Emotional beat: terror and unwilling responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The map speaks — the voice of Veyra, a cartographer executed a century ago, her memory bound to the parchment. She calls Orsen 'heir' and shows her the road to the Emberhold. The guild's master, Sable Fenwick, reveals the guild has guarded the map's existence for generations. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Through the guildmaster's eyes we learn the guild once served dragons, not thieves, and that Orsen's family name appears in the oldest ledger — Delacroix, 'fire-sworn.' Sable hides this from her, fearing what she'll do with it. Emotional beat: guilt of a keeper of secrets.

chapters.title: White Cloaks in the Wheat
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Fleeing along the pilgrim road, Orsen and Veyra's voice are ambushed by Ashen hunters. She survives by instinctively swallowing a toxin meant to paralyze her — her immunity deepening, her dragonblood stirring. A hunter recognizes the Delacroix name before dying. Emotional beat: first taste of her own power, and fear of it.

chapters.title: The City That Burned Its Name
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Sheltering in Cindermark, a city built atop a dragon's grave, Orsen learns from ash-priests how the ancient war ended: not in victory, but in a bargain — human fire-tasters bred to hold dragonfire in trust. Her lineage is the bargain's collateral. Emotional beat: grief for an inheritance weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Sable's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Cornered by the Ashen Order, Sable trades the guild's secrets for Orsen's location, believing surrendering the map will save everyone. Alone in the ransacked counting-house, he reads the first ledger aloud to an empty room — a confession no one hears. Emotional beat: betrayal committed out of love.

chapters.title: The Emberhold
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Captured and dragged to the Emberhold by the Order's Grand Ashen, Orsen is shown the last dragon-fire guttering in its iron cradle — and told the truth: extinguish it, and no war can ever burn again. Veyra's memory begins to fray as the fire dims. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of ending everything.

chapters.title: Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. At the cradle, Orsen refuses both options — hoard the fire or kill it — and instead drinks it, taking the ember into her dragonblood body as Veyra's memory dissolves into her own. The Grand Ashen strikes; Sable arrives with the guild to hold the line and falls buying her the moment she needs. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into choice.

chapters.title: Thorn and Spire
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Carrying the fire within her, Orsen stands before the Crown that poisoned her and offers new terms: the fire will be shared, sworn freely, not owned. Dragons begin to wake across the world, choosing their allies. She reopens the ledgers under a new heading — inheritances returned. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, justice outside the law.
